newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony shares fall sharply on yen's rise.
newsitem.headline: Sony shares fall sharply on yen's rise.

text.p: Shares in Sony Corp dropped sharply in early Tokyo trading on Monday on the yen's rapid rally against the dollar, brokers said.
As of 0014 GMT, the shares were down 170 yen at 9,350 yen with turnover of 688,600.

"The rapid rally of the yen spurred sales (in Sony shares) but since the company used a dollar/yen rate of 115 yen in making its earnings estimates unveiled recently, the yen has not yet risen high enough to be a major selling factor. I think we still can buy the shares on dips," said one trader at a major securities firm.

Sony hit a record intraday high of 9,830 yen on Friday, a day after unveiling robust earnings results for the last business year. Sony was among Japan's major export-orientated blue-chips, which benefitted from the yen's weakness in the past two years.
Sony's group net profit in the year to March 31 was 139.46 billion yen, 2.6 times up on the year before, while parent current profit was 85.73 billion yen, a three-fold rise from the previous year.
"The shares are seen moving into an adjustment phase. I think they will likely face about 10 percent slippage from their peak levels," said one official at another big brokerage.
